task.description: Validate src/design/iss0176-lua07-audit-manifest-hash-minimal-wiring.md for GH-504/ISS-0176 (LUA-07 criterion 2). This design implements a HUMAN-OPERATOR-CONFIRMED scope decision (do not re-litigate whether minimal synthetic wiring is the right call -- that decision was made explicitly outside the pipeline). Your job is to validate the DESIGN's technical correctness and honesty, not the scope decision itself. Verify independently: (1) the design's core claim -- that no engine call site currently invokes the Lua executor -- re-confirm via your own grep of src/engine/ for ScriptResult/executeScript; (2) the EXT-03 plugin-registry rejection reasoning (design section 2.1) -- confirm registerGlobalPluginHandler/registerPluginHandler really are called only from test files, never from src/main.zig or any production bootstrap, by checking yourself; (3) confirm recordExecutionErrorEventInTx (cited as the closest existing precedent for this function's transaction-boundary convention) genuinely exists at the cited location in src/engine/instance.zig with the signature/behavior described; (4) confirm the audit-table schema decision (new dedicated table vs the two rejected alternatives) is well-reasoned against the ACTUAL schemas of audit_entries and audit_log -- read both migration files yourself; (5) confirm the mutation-test design (section 5) is genuinely mutation-checkable as claimed -- would deleting the INSERT or its manifest_hash binding actually make the test fail, or is there a gap in the reasoning; (6) confirm the design's honesty framing (the doc-comment text prescribed for the new function, explicitly stating it is NOT the SERVICE_TASK handler) is precise enough that BACKEND-DEV cannot accidentally under- or over-state what was built when writing the actual code; (7) confirm no implementation code beyond illustrative signatures is present (Type E per templates/lego-catalog.md).
acceptance_criteria: EXT-03 rejection reasoning independently confirmed against actual call sites
recordExecutionErrorEventInTx precedent confirmed to genuinely exist as cited
Audit-table schema decision confirmed well-reasoned against actual existing schemas
Honesty framing confirmed precise and unambiguous for BACKEND-DEV to implement faithfully
No implementation code beyond illustrative Type E signatures

result.summary: Independently re-verified all 5 technical claims in src/design/iss0176-lua07-audit-manifest-hash-minimal-wiring.md and all were confirmed accurate: (1) grep of src/engine/ for ScriptResult|executeScript returns zero matches -- no engine call site invokes the Lua executor today; (2) registerGlobalPluginHandler/registerPluginHandler are called only from tests/unit/ext03_plugin_test.zig and tests/integration/{ext03_plugin_integration_test,svc02_plugin_dispatch_scope_test,svc03_definition_activation_scope_test}.zig -- zero matches in src/main.zig or any production bootstrap; processServiceTaskRuntimeInTx (instance.zig:2858) calls plugin_registry_mod.resolveGlobalPluginHandler('SERVICE_TASK') at line 2896, confirming EXT-03 is real wired dispatch with no production registration -- rejection reasoning holds; (3) recordExecutionErrorEventInTx exists at instance.zig:3470 exactly as described: takes conn: *db.Conn, performs no BEGIN/COMMIT, issues one $1..$4-parameterised INSERT; (4) read both migrations/020_obs03_audit_entries.sql and migrations/009_audit_log.sql in full -- audit_entries is confirmed populated exclusively by bpm_audit_on_mutation() triggers on 8 named business tables (none of which a Lua execution mutates), and audit_log.detail is a free-form JSONB column with no typed hash column -- the new-dedicated-table decision is well-reasoned against the real schemas; (5) the mutation-test design (Sec.5) is genuinely mutation-checkable -- step 5's SELECT...WHERE audit_id=$1 assertion can only pass if the INSERT and its manifest_hash binding both actually ran, confirmed by reading ScriptResult/ExecutionContext/ScriptManifest in src/lua/executor.zig and src/lua/manifest.zig, whose real field types (instance_id: []const u8, manifest_hash: [32]u8/?[32]u8, ScriptResult.deinit) match every illustrative signature in the design verbatim. Additionally confirmed: no implementation code beyond illustrative Type E signatures (only 2 code blocks in the file, both bare declarations ending in ';' with no bodies; SQL in Sec.3.2 is numbered prose, not a DDL code block); classification as Type E is correct per templates/lego-catalog.md (audit chain / cross-cutting engine logic is explicitly listed as never-templated); tools/lint_design_artefact.py exits 0 with no issues. LUA-07's requirements.yaml entry independently confirms the scope match ('Manifest hash MUST be recorded with each execution' / criterion 2 'appears in the execution audit record') and that ScriptResult's own existing doc comment in executor.zig already anticipates this exact follow-up ('persisting it into the execution audit record is the engine's job... See design Sec.6.4 and Sec.11 follow-up 2'). HOWEVER: found one concrete, load-bearing honesty-framing defect (claim 6) that fails the design as written. The prescribed doc comment in Sec.2.2, which the design explicitly instructs BACKEND-DEV to 'preserve' verbatim, states executeScriptForAudit 'persists the resulting manifest_hash to audit_entries' (line 108) -- but Sec.3.1/3.2 explicitly REJECT audit_entries as the write target and choose a new dedicated table, lua_script_execution_audit, instead (with detailed, correct reasoning). Every other reference in the document (Sec.3.1, 3.2, 5, 6, 7 -- verified by grep, 13 occurrences total) consistently and correctly names lua_script_execution_audit; only the doc-comment text at line 108 names the wrong table. If BACKEND-DEV preserves this framing verbatim as instructed, the shipped function's own doc comment will permanently misstate where the audit row is written -- directly undermining Sec.2.3's stated purpose for that comment ('the durable record of this fact so a future reader does not mistake ...'). A secondary, milder instance of the same slip: the illustrative migration filename given in the header (line 5) and Sec.3.2 ('migrations/0NN_iss0176_audit_entries_manifest_hash.sql') also embeds 'audit_entries' despite the table being lua_script_execution_audit -- cosmetic since BACKEND-DEV assigns the real filename, but reinforces the same naming confusion and should be corrected in the same pass.

issues.description: Sec.2.2's prescribed doc comment (line 108) states executeScriptForAudit persists manifest_hash to 'audit_entries', contradicting Sec.3.1/3.2's explicit, correct, and unchanged decision to use a new dedicated table 'lua_script_execution_audit' instead (audit_entries is trigger-fed only per migration 020 and is explicitly rejected as a target). This is the exact text the design instructs BACKEND-DEV to preserve verbatim, so implementing it as written ships a doc comment that permanently misstates the write target -- undermining the comment's own stated purpose in Sec.2.3 of being 'the durable record of this fact'. Fix: replace 'audit_entries' with 'lua_script_execution_audit' at line 108.

The illustrative migration filename in the document header (line 5) and Sec.3.2 ('migrations/0NN_iss0176_audit_entries_manifest_hash.sql') names 'audit_entries' despite the table being 'lua_script_execution_audit'. Cosmetic (BACKEND-DEV assigns the real migration number/name per Sec.3.2's own instruction), but reinforces the same table-name confusion as ISS-0176-DESIGN-REVIEW-1 and should be corrected in the same rework pass, e.g. 'migrations/0NN_iss0176_lua_script_execution_audit.sql'.

result.next_action: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER for rework: fix Sec.2.2 doc-comment table-name reference (line 108) from 'audit_entries' to 'lua_script_execution_audit', and optionally correct the illustrative migration filename in the header and Sec.3.2 to match. All other technical claims independently verified as accurate; this is a single-line-plus-cosmetic fix, not a structural rework.
